title: When Dinosaurs Lived, a Day Was Only 23.5 Hours

scenes.text: When dinosaurs lived, a day was only 23 and a half hours long.
The Earth is slowing down, because the Moon is slowly pulling away from us, about 3.8 centimetres every year.
Scientists proved it with a 70-million-year-old seashell.
Its growth rings showed 372 days in a year, which means each day was shorter.
Days have been getting longer ever since, by about two milliseconds per century.
Enjoy your 24 hours. Future humans will get even more.

description:
A 70-million-year-old shell showed a year had 372 days, so each day was about 23.5 hours.
The Moon's pull is slowing Earth's spin, so days keep getting longer.
What would you do with an extra hour?
